The <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span> is a service that accepts HTTPS requests with
latitude/longitude coordinates for one or more points on a map. It uses these
points to find nearby road segments and returns a Place ID along with metadata
such as the nearest road segment and speed limits.

<h2 id="why" data-text="Why use the Roads API" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">Why use the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span></span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: Why use the Roads API" data-title="Copy link to this section: Why use the Roads API" data-id="why"></button></h2>

<p>With the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span>, you can get speed limits, estimated
arrival times, or other road metadata. With this road
metadata, you can enhance your driving apps with the follow capabilities:</p>

<ul>
<li>Connect latitude/longitude coordinates with a road or roads.</li>
<li>Find the nearest road for a set of coordinates</li>
<li>Get speed limits for road segments</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="what" data-text="What you can do with the Roads API" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">What you can do with the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span></span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: What you can do with the Roads API" data-title="Copy link to this section: What you can do with the Roads API" data-id="what"></button></h2>

<p>With the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span>, you can map GPS coordinates to the
geometry of the road, and determine the speed limit along road
segments.</p>

<ul>
<li><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap">Snap to Roads</a></strong> This service returns the most likely
roads traveled based on the provided set of GPS coordinates. You can specify
up to 100 GPS points collected along a route. Optionally,
you can also request that the service interpolates additional points,
resulting in a path that smoothly follows the geometry of the road.</li>
<li><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/nearest">Nearest Roads</a></strong> This service returns the nearest
road segment for a GPS point. You can specify up to 100
GPS points. The points you specify don't need to be part of a continuous
path.</li>
<li><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/speed-limits">Speed limits</a></strong> This service returns the posted
speed limit for a road segment. The Speed Limit service is available to all
customers with an Asset Tracking license. For <a href="/maps/premium">Google Maps Platform Premium Plan</a>
customers who transitioned to pay-as-you-go pricing, the feature remains
active.</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="works" data-text="How the Roads API works" tabindex="-1" role="presentation"><span class="devsite-heading" role="heading" aria-level="2">How the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span> works</span><button type="button" class="devsite-heading-link button-flat material-icons" aria-label="Copy link to this section: How the Roads API works" data-title="Copy link to this section: How the Roads API works" data-id="works"></button></h2>

<p>The <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span> uses three endpoints which accept latitude/longitude
coordinates or place IDs to provide road paths, segments, or speed limit data.
The following example shows a request for nearest roads based on a set
of latitude/longitude coordinates:</p>

<h3 id="resources" data-text="Resources" tabindex="-1">Resources</h3>

<p>The following table summarizes the resources available through the
<span class="notranslate">Roads API</span> along with the data it returns.</p>

<p></p><div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table class="fixed">
    <tbody><tr>
      <th>Data resources</th>
      <th>Data returned</th>
      <th width="20%">Return format</th>
     </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap">Snap to roads</a></strong>
       </td>
     <td>
        <p>Returns an array of up to 100 GPS points from a route. Includes
        road-snapped longitude/latitude coordinates along
        with place IDs. See details in
        <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap#responses">Responses</a>
        in the <u>Snap to roads</u>
        guide.</p>
      </td>
      <td rowspan="3">
       <ul>
         <li>JSON</li>
       </ul>
        </td>
      </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/nearest">Nearest roads</a></strong>
      </td>
     <td>
        <p>An array of up to 100 independent latitude/longitude coordinates
        along with place IDs for the nearest road for each specified point.
        Points do not need to be continuous. See details in
        <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/nearest#responses">Responses</a>
        in the <u>Nearest roads</u>
        guide.</p>
      </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td><strong><a href="/maps/documentation/roads/speed-limits">Speed limits</a></strong>
      </td>
     <td>
        <p>An array of up to 100 road metadata elements. These contain speed
        limits and place IDs, with units either in KPH or MPH. See details
        in <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/nearest#responses">Responses</a>
        in the <u>Speed limits</u>
        guide.</p>
      </td>
   </tr>
  </tbody></table></div><p></p>

<h2 id="how" data-text="How to use the Roads API" tabindex="-1">How to use the <span class="notranslate">Roads API</span></h2>

<div class="devsite-table-wrapper"><table class="implementation-path">
 <tbody><tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">1</span></td>
    <td><strong>Try the snap to roads demo</strong></td>
    <td>Click the demo to create a track and see how the snap to roads endpoint
    provides smooth data. See
     <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap#demo">Demo</a>
      in the <strong>Snap to roads</strong> guide. You don't need an API key.
    </td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">2</span></td>
    <td><strong>Get set up</strong></td>
    <td>Start with <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/cloud-setup">Set up your
        Google Cloud project</a> and complete the setup instructions that follow
        and then learn
        <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/get-api-key">how to use your API key</a>.
    </td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">3</span></td>
    <td><strong>Try a snap to roads request</strong></td>
    <td>
     <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap#examples">Use one of the snap
     to roads examples</a> and try one relevant to your use case.
    </td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">4</span></td>
    <td><strong>Get speed limits for your road path</strong></td>
    <td>Using the same path data you provided for your snap to roads request,
    issue a speed limit query. See the
     <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/speed-limits#example_request_using_a_path">Example request using a path</a>.
    </td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">5</span></td>
    <td><strong>Learn how to process long paths</strong></td>
    <td>Follow the sections on
     <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/advanced#processing_long_paths">Processing long paths</a>
     in the <strong>Advanced concepts</strong> guide.
    </td>
  </tr>
 <tr>
    <td><span class="numbered">6</span></td>
    <td><strong>Incorporate road data into your own app!</strong></td>
    <td>See the
    <a href="/maps/documentation/roads/snap#javascript-+-html">detailed code example</a> from the road snapped demo to start
    building road data functionality into your own app.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody></table></div>

<h3 id="available_client_libraries" data-text="Available client libraries" tabindex="-1">Available client libraries</h3>

<p>Call this API in the language of
your choice through one of the following client libraries:</p>

  <ul>
      <li><a href="https://github.com/googlemaps/google-maps-services-java" class="external">Java
  Client for Google Maps Services</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://github.com/googlemaps/google-maps-services-python" class="external">Python
  Client for Google Maps Services</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://github.com/googlemaps/google-maps-services-go" class="external">Go Client
  for Google Maps Services</a></li>
      <li><a href="https://github.com/googlemaps/google-maps-services-js" class="external">Node.js
  Client for Google Maps Services</a></li>
    </ul>

<p>The Java Client, Python Client, Go Client and Node.js Client for Google Maps
Services are community-supported client libraries, open sourced under the
<a href="http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0" class="external">Apache 2.0 License</a>.
Download them from GitHub, where you can also find installation instructions and sample code.</p>
